messages:
maria: quick q — we keep hitting a hard decision point: when an upstream model node dies midstream, do we prefer buffering at the edge and attempting transparent resume, or to fast-fail and rely on client-side retry windows?

sam: +1 for surfacing the tradeoffs. buffering/resume keeps client UX smooth but increases memory and complexity (resume tokens, prefix KV state). fast-fail is simpler and keeps gateway stateless.

jin: from quality POV resume is nice — users get partial + continue. but if the model variant changes on failover we risk semantic drift (different completions). idempotency + tokenization matters.

kevin: operational concerns: buffering needs bounded memory per connection. we saw a POC blow OOM when many long chats were midflight. we need a hard cap and eviction strategy. also: what about billing? if we replay tokens to a different model we double-count.

maria: thoughts on a middle path: keep a small prefix cache (last N tokens / last M bytes) + a short resume window (e.g., 10s / 2KB). outside that, fast-fail. This reduces worst-case memory yet enables quick restarts for transient failures.

sam: config sketch:
```
edge.retry: {
  resume_window_secs: 10,
  resume_prefix_bytes: 2048,
  max_buffer_per_conn: 256KB,
  resume_strict_model_match: true, // only resume to identical model spec
  fallback: fast_fail
}
```

jin: +1 for resume_strict_model_match. if model differs we should bubble a clear error so clients can choose to retry with tolerance.

kevin: also add metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success, buffer_evictions, double_charge_alerts. we should trigger alert if resume_success < 80% after deploys (indicates mismatch behavior).

maria: what about semantics for streaming trailers? if we resume do we append new tokens or mark a gap? clients expect a contiguous stream. maybe send a small JSON trailer marker: `{\"resumed\":true, \"gap_bytes\":N}` so client-side can decide.

sam: agreed. trailer marker is lightweight. also need a deterministic resume token fingerprint: hash(prefix + request_id + model_version) so we can verify compatibility at restart.

kevin: failure modes: a) upstream crash during KV flush -> resume token invalid b) partial send to client -> can we dedupe? we should attach monotonic chunk ids to streaming frames so proxies downstream can drop duplicates.

jin: chunk ids + resume trailer works. but warn teams: if you depend on side effects (DB writes) midstream, resume semantics must be conservative -> prefer fast-fail or require exactly-once backend handles.

maria: action items: 1) sam to draft edge config RFC with above param names and default values. 2) kevin to list required metrics/alerts + memory caps. 3) jin to write a short client contract for resume trailers & chunk ids.

deploy-bot: scheduled: edge-config-rfc-draft created by sam in #architecture -> link: https://go/repo/edge-config-rfc (internal).

kevin: one more: let's gate resume by tenancy: dedicated customers might want bigger resume windows; hosted should default conservative. note per-tenant limits in RFC.

maria: yeah good point. ok I'll consolidate and we can sync Wed 11am. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
